news_drafts.headline: Caerphilly faces £2.867m budget overspend and schools crisis reaching £14.127m deficit by 2028
news_drafts.lead: Caerphilly Council expects to spend £506.476m against a revised budget of £503.609m in 2026/27, leaving a shortfall of £2.867m. Adult Services is overspending by £0.709m and Children's Services by £0.497m, driven by demand-led pressures. The council planned to fill this gap through savings, but its £12.33m savings programme is running 22 percent off-track, with £2.67m of the savings either undelivered or at risk. Schools reserves (money the council has set aside for schools' day-to-day costs) are already in deficit by £0.374m and are forecast to reach a deficit of £14.127m by March 2028, remaining at that level through 2030. Because these reserves are separate from the council's main budget, they cannot be covered by other council spending, leaving a funding gap that the council does not expect to recover.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Multiple services reporting unachievable income targets, including Parks overspend of £0.379m
findings.detail: Parks and Countryside reports a £0.379m overspend driven by persistent pressures with pitch fees and income targets that have not materialised. Across the council, multiple services underachieve income: Waste continues to report income shortfalls, capital fee income has reduced due to fewer projects, and Fleet Services underachieves targets due to reduced demand following higher charges.
findings.matters: Councils with systematic income underachievement across multiple services may face forecasting problems or demand assumptions issues; if many services cannot achieve planned income, this suggests overoptimistic budgeting that could materialise as further overspends.
findings.figures: Parks and Countryside £0.379m overspend; Waste income underachievement (unspecified); capital fee income reduced (fewer projects); Fleet Services underachievement (reduced demand, lost contract income)
findings.quote: Parks and Countryside which includes cemeteries are anticipating £0.379m overspend. There are year on year pressures with pitch fees and other unachievable income targets which are being addressed as part of the transformation programme.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Temporary Accommodation remains under overspend pressure despite targeted mitigation activity
findings.detail: Temporary Accommodation is forecasting a £0.257m Q1 overspend despite active mitigation efforts: closure of a large out-of-county facility, creation of 23 new bed spaces since February 2026, and security contract reviews generating £0.440m savings. However, Housing Benefit subsidy recoverability has reduced from 20% to 16%, and demand remains sustained with wider national pressures noted.
findings.matters: Temporary Accommodation is a discretionary social care cost that grows with homelessness demand; continued overspend despite targeted mitigation suggests the cost driver (demand) is not being addressed and will continue to drain resources.
findings.figures: £0.257m Q1 overspend; £0.440m projected saving from security contract review; 23 new bed spaces created since February 2026; Housing Benefit subsidy recoverability 16% (down from 20%)
findings.quote: Housing is projecting an overspend of £0.257m which is predominantly from an increased spend forecast for Temporary Accommodation reflecting sustained demand and wider national pressures.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: MTFP projects £8.457m structural budget gap with underlying demand exceeding available resources
findings.detail: The Medium Term Financial Plan presented at budget setting identified an unresolved gap of £8.457m for 2027/28-2028/29 under base case assumptions, rising to £28.712m in worst-case scenarios. The council states that demand and cost growth are exceeding available resources in several key service areas. Key unresolved pressures include ALN, social care, temporary accommodation and home to school transport.
findings.matters: An unresolved MTFP gap of £8.457m over two years indicates the council's underlying revenue budget is unsustainable and raises questions about whether it can remain solvent without reserve depletion or service reductions.
findings.figures: £8.457m gap (base case 2027/28-2028/29); £28.712m gap (worst case scenario); key pressures: ALN, social care, temporary accommodation, home to school transport
findings.quote: The MTFP as presented at budget setting for 2026/27 had a gap of £8.457m for the following 2 years.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: Demand-led overspends in social care and transport totalling £4.4m forecast to escalate
findings.detail: Adult social care is experiencing major demand pressures: residential care overspending by £3.235m and support for children with disabilities by £0.603m, while children's services face £0.402m pressure from increased looked-after children numbers. Additionally, home to school transport is overrunning by £0.676m driven by ALN transport requirements and contract inflation. The council notes these demand pressures are expected to continue and escalate through the medium term.
findings.matters: Demand-led cost growth that outpaces available resources is structural and harder to control than input inflation; if demand pressures persist as forecast, reserves will deplete faster than planned.
findings.figures: Adult residential care £3.235m; children with disabilities support £0.603m; children looked after £0.402m; home to school transport £0.676m (5.17% overspend)
findings.quote: the division has experienced a significant increase in demand for residential care for adults at a cost of £3.235m along with additional demand for support for children with disabilities at a cost of £0.603m.

findings.paper_title: Whole Authority Revenue Budget Monitoring Report (Quarter One).
findings.headline: School balance sheet faces £4.358m projected collective deficit with structural cost base problems
findings.detail: Caerphilly's school sector is projecting a collective deficit of £4.358m at year-end, with 30 schools in deficit positions (23 primary, 7 secondary reporting deficits). The paper identifies falling pupil numbers and significant surplus capacity as the underlying structural cause. Without sustainable solutions through the school estate review, deficits are forecast to increase significantly over the medium term.
findings.matters: School deficits accumulate as a draw on council reserves and reduce financial resilience; a £4.358m balance sheet charge and forecast increases threaten medium-term solvency if the structural issues are not resolved.
findings.figures: £4.358m net deficit projected (primary surplus £1.724m offset by secondary/middle/special deficit £6.082m); 30 schools in deficit (including 23 primary and 7 secondary)
findings.quote: This is a net deficit position of £4.358m. The continuing deterioration in school balances highlights the need to address underlying structural pressures within the education system.

daily_post.headline: Commercial estate income recovery is at risk; £100k of £200k saving is Amber
daily_post.lead: Council borrowing and financial standing often depends on property income. An income plan that is 50% uncertain in Q1 signals asset performance or market conditions are worse than budgeted.
